related_questions.question: What diseases does Cryptococcus neoformans cause?
related_questions.snippet: Overview. Cryptococcosis is a fungal disease caused by breathing in spores from Cryptococcus, a fungus found in the environment. The infection can affect the different parts of the body but usually causes lung or brain infections (cryptococcal meningitis). Different species are found in different parts of the world.

related_questions.snippet: Cryptococcosis can affect the lungs (pneumonia) and nervous system (meningitis) in humans. It affects people with healthy and weakened immune system. In rare cases, this disease can be fatal. Each year in B.C., 10-25 people become sick from cryptococcosis and about 16% die from the disease.

text_blocks.snippet: Cryptococcus neoformans causes cryptococcosis, a fungal infection that can manifest in various forms, most notably cryptococcal meningitis. This infection primarily affects the central nervous system, leading to inflammation of the brain and spinal cord. Additionally, cryptococcosis can affect the lungs, skin, and other organs.

list.title: Cryptococcal Meningitis:
list.snippet: This is the most common and serious manifestation, characterized by inflammation of the meninges (membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord). Symptoms can include headache, fever, stiff neck, and neurological changes. In severe cases, it can lead to brain damage, coma, and even death if left untreated.

list.title: Lung Infections:
list.snippet: Cryptococcosis can also cause pneumonia-like symptoms, such as cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain.

list.title: Cutaneous Cryptococcosis:
list.snippet: Skin involvement can occur, with lesions appearing as nodules, ulcers, or papules. This is more common in individuals with weakened immune systems.

list.title: Other Organs:
list.snippet: In some cases, the infection can spread to other organs, including the prostate and other tissues.

text_blocks.snippet: Cryptococcosis is particularly dangerous for individuals with weakened immune systems, such as those with HIV/AIDS, those on long-term corticosteroid therapy, or those who have undergone organ transplants. For people with HIV, cryptococcosis is a defining opportunistic infection, often associated with low CD4 cell counts.
